hero.headline: $70 million K-8 school breaks ground in Fort Pierce, will consolidate three St. Lucie County schools
hero.body:
A groundbreaking ceremony marked the start of construction on a new K-8 school in Fort Pierce that will combine three St. Lucie County schools into one facility. The new school will be built on land behind Dan McCarty Middle School and is expected to welcome between 1,500 and 1,800 students when it opens. It will consolidate Dan McCarty Middle, St. Lucie Elementary and Lawnwood Elementary into a single campus.

Superintendent Jon Prince said the project is moving forward on time and on budget. The new facility will feature state-of-the-art technology and serve the north part of St. Lucie County. The decision to consolidate comes as the existing schools show their age. All three were built in the 1950s and 1960s. Dan McCarty Middle Principal Latricia Stubbs-James said some of the things inside the building are antiquated.

The district is funding the $70 million project in part by selling the properties where the three older schools currently stand, offsetting the cost of maintaining aging buildings. Prince said the K-8 model is already proven across the district, which operates 11 other K-8 schools. Attendance is better, test scores are better and grades are better in the K-8s, Prince said. Stubbs-James said the K-8 model offers unique benefits, allowing kindergarten students to see what it looks like to be an eighth grader.

The new Fort Pierce K-8 school is expected to be completed in August 2028.

cards.headline: Mother, grandfather, and girlfriend arrested after 3-month-old dies from dehydration and malnutrition in Fort Pierce
cards.teaser: Three people face aggravated manslaughter and child abuse charges after a 3-month-old boy died from dehydration and malnutrition in a Fort Pierce mobile home last August.
cards.body:
The St. Lucie County Sheriffs Office arrested Nicole Maxwell, her father Robert Maxwell, and his girlfriend Vikki Koon nearly a year after the infant's death. The baby died in August 2025 after living primarily with Robert Maxwell and Koon while his mother lived at her boyfriend's home in Vero Beach. Detective Jennifer Diaz said in her 20 years of law enforcement, this is one of the worst cases she has ever worked.

According to court documents, Koon told deputies she believed a newborn should have two ounces per feeding twice a day. When she ran out of formula, she would fill the bottle with regular milk and add water. An autopsy revealed the infant was emaciated and had a sunken abdomen and widespread lesions consistent with severe dehydration and malnutrition. The medical examiner ruled the death a homicide.

Investigators described the mobile home as extremely hot with a bug infestation, lack of food, and unsafe conditions for walking. A neighbor named Suzan said she had concerns about the children's living conditions and would give two of the boys food and drinks when they knocked on her door. Nicole Maxwell's other children who were living in the mobile home are now in foster care. The case took nearly a year to complete because of the complexity and the need for outside medical experts.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce police seek help identifying vandalism and burglary suspects in two separate investigations
cards.teaser: Fort Pierce police are asking for the public's help identifying people shown in surveillance images connected to vandalism at the Fort Pierce Recreation Center and vehicle burglaries in the Lawnwood Circle area.
cards.body:
Police said the vandalism occurred at about 4 p.m. July 24 at the Fort Pierce Recreation Center, located at 903 S. An unidentified woman was captured on camera damaging city property. Multiple air-conditioning units, a trailer and a storage shed were damaged.

The second investigation involves a series of vehicle burglaries reported during the overnight hours of July 27 in the Lawnwood Circle area. Police said the burglaries occurred in the 1300 block of Nebraska Avenue and the 1300 block of Peppertree Trail, primarily between 2 a.m. Several vehicles were burglarized. Some had been left unlocked, while others had windows smashed to gain entry. Surveillance footage showed several people in the area wearing hoodies, shorts and backpacks. Anyone who recognizes the people pictured or has information about either case is asked to contact Fort Pierce police at 772-467-6800 or 772-462-6800.

cards.headline: Man forced to withdraw cash during armed robbery at Wells Fargo ATM in Fort Pierce
cards.teaser: Two men forced a customer to withdraw cash at gunpoint from a Wells Fargo ATM in Fort Pierce on Sunday night before fleeing on foot.
cards.body:
The Fort Pierce Police Department said the robbery happened Sunday at about 8:38 p.m. Two men approached the victim, and one of them displayed a gun concealed in his waistband before forcing the victim to withdraw an unknown amount of cash.

Officers with the Fort Pierce Police Department responded to the scene, established a perimeter, and used a K-9 and drone to search for the suspects. The suspects were not located. Police described them as two men in their early 20s, about 5 feet 10 inches tall and weighing about 170 pounds. The armed suspect was last seen wearing jeans and a gray hooded sweatshirt.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie opens $28.8 million police training facility with indoor firing range and tactical shoot house
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie cut the ribbon on a 54,283-square-foot police training center on July 24 after four years of construction, featuring a 20-lane indoor firing range and tactical shoot house.
cards.body:
The $28.8 million police training center is on the Port St. Lucie City Hall grounds, just northwest of the police department. Mayor Shannon Martin said making Port St. Lucie the safest large city in Florida takes more than dedication and requires planning ahead and making smart investments that prepare officers for the challenges they face every day.

The three-story facility includes a 20-lane, 9,508-square-foot indoor firearms range featuring an integrated MILO live-fire scenario system. It also has a 2,848-square-foot tactical shoot house with configurable rooms for realistic scenario-based training and a MILO Virtual Simulation Theater for immersive decision-making and de-escalation exercises. The facility includes a dedicated defensive tactics training room equipped with Axon VR technology and three floors of office space supporting the Training Division and Criminal Investigations Division, including 19 offices and 86 workstations. For years, officers traveled to Indian River State College in Fort Pierce for extensive training.

cards.headline: Two men flee Port St. Lucie police at 80 mph, one found hiding on roof of occupied home
cards.teaser: A suspected drunk driver fled Port St. Lucie police at nearly 80 mph in a 45 mph zone before he and his passenger abandoned their car and ran, with one suspect later found hiding on the roof of an occupied home.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie police attempted to stop a white Acura after observing multiple traffic violations and signs of impaired driving. Instead of pulling over, the driver accelerated to nearly 80 mph in a 45 mph zone on Southwest Becker Road. The driver and passenger weaved in and out of traffic, ignored traffic signs and signals, then abandoned the vehicle in a residential driveway near Southwest Idol Avenue before fleeing on foot.

A nearby resident called 911 after seeing the two men run from the scene. Police deployed a K-9 and a drone while officers established a perimeter. Both suspects were located, including one who was found hiding on the roof of an occupied home. The suspects were identified as Joseph Gary Harris, 42, and Bryan Shawn Baker, 46. Harris was charged with fleeing and eluding law enforcement, burglary of an occupied dwelling, resisting an officer without violence, and loitering or prowling. Baker was charged with resisting an officer without violence and loitering or prowling.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie could lose $48 million in property tax revenue if November ballot measure passes
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie is preparing for a potential $48 million loss in property tax revenue over the next two years if a constitutional amendment on the November 3 ballot passes.
cards.body:
City Manager Jesus Merejo told the City Council the city would lose over $48 million in property taxes over the next two years if Amendment 3 passes in November. To prepare for the potential hit, the city is holding the line on hiring and deferring projects. Port St. Lucie will not fund 184 requested positions, worth $28.3 million, including 25 new police officers and parks staff the city had already planned to add this year to keep up with growth at Torino Regional Park and the new BMX facility at Tradition Regional Park.

The $7.8 million in canceled projects includes a study for a new interchange connecting Marshall Parkway to I-95, an inclusive playground at McChesney Park, and parking improvements at Riverland Paseo Park, along with construction on a new City Hall and parking garage. The police department's budget is actually going up nearly 10%, to just under $104 million, driven mostly by a 5% contractual raise for sworn officers along with new equipment, training and technology upgrades. City employees will not get a cost-of-living raise in the coming budget. Amendment 3 would raise the state's homestead exemption from $50,000 to $150,000 starting in January 2027, and to $250,000 in January 2028. It needs at least 60% approval from voters to pass.

hero.headline: Indian River County Fire Rescue mourns death of firefighter Geoffrey Lang who died Saturday
hero.teaser: Indian River County Fire Rescue announced the death of Firefighter and Paramedic Geoffrey Lang, who died following what officials described as a personal tragedy at his Sebastian home.
hero.body:
Lang died Saturday, according to a news release from Indian River County Fire Rescue. Lang joined Indian River County Fire Rescue in 2015 and served the community for more than a decade. County officials said he was known for his professionalism, compassion and dedication to serving others. He is survived by his wife, two children and his parents.

Fire Chief David Johnson said Lang faithfully served the community for more than a decade and his absence will be deeply felt throughout the department. County Administrator John A. said the county's thoughts are with Lang's family, friends and fellow firefighters during this difficult time.

County Commission Chairman Deryl Loar extended condolences on behalf of the Board of County Commissioners and emphasized the county's commitment to supporting the mental health and well-being of first responders and their families. Indian River County Fire Rescue asked the public to respect the privacy of Lang's family, friends and colleagues as they grieve.

cards.headline: Sebastian police, Vero Beach police extend condolences after death of Indian River County firefighter

cards.teaser: The Vero Beach Police Department said it stands with Indian River County Fire Rescue following the death of Firefighter Geoffrey Lang.
cards.body:
The Vero Beach Police Department said it stands alongside Indian River County Fire Rescue in mourning the loss of Firefighter Geoffrey Lang, who passed away while off duty. The department said its thoughts are with his family, loved ones and colleagues during this incredibly difficult time and that it honors his service and the impact he made on the community.

 Indian River County Fire Rescue announced Lang's death Saturday night and thanked neighboring agencies that quickly shared messages of support following the announcement. The Sebastian Police Department said it stands alongside its brothers and sisters of Indian River County Fire Rescue as they mourn the heartbreaking loss and that Lang's dedication, courage and commitment to serving others will never be forgotten.

cards.headline: Discarded fishing line transformed into friendship bracelets at Vero Beach Museum of Art

cards.body:
The Vero Beach Museum of Art and Coastal Connections will team up for a free Second Saturday program beginning at 10 a.m. Aug. 8, featuring hands-on activities, gallery tours and lessons about protecting local marine life. Coastal Connections will lead an activity in the Laura and Bill Buck Atrium where visitors can make friendship bracelets using recycled fishing line collected from local waterways. Participants can also learn about the organization's Fishing Line Recycling Program.

 The museum has adopted the fishing line recycling tube at the Riverside Park boat ramp. From 10 a.m. to 1 p.m., families can take short, docent-led gallery tours through the Museum Studios family program. Visitors can then participate in Nature in Layers, an art activity for children connected to the museum's exhibitions.

 Guests can also tour the museum's summer exhibitions throughout the day. James Prosek: At Work is on view in the Holmes Gallery, while Jill Nathanson: Chromatic Phrases is displayed in the Schumann and Titelman galleries. Second Saturday includes free museum admission throughout the day.

 Kendra Bergman, founder and executive director of Coastal Connections, said the partnership is an example of how the organization is working with the community to introduce everyone to marine conservation and environmental protection in unique ways. Coastal Connections was founded in 2017 with a mission of advancing the survival of sea turtles by educating and connecting people to the environment.
